svg.title: Four generations of the function g-theta, one fixed softmax head
svg.desc: Four rows showing how a prefix becomes next-token probabilities P of x_j given the earlier tokens. Row 1, n-gram counting: a window of the last n minus 1 tokens indexes a lookup table whose row is the stored distribution, fitted by counting; there is no representation h_j and no softmax head. Row 2, neural n-gram: the window tokens become embedding vectors fed through a neural network to h_j, then a linear and softmax head. Row 3, RNN or LSTM: tokens are read one at a time and each updates a hidden state in a chain to h_j, then the same head. Row 4, Transformer: every earlier token connects to h_j with attention arrows of varying thickness, then the same head. From row 2 on, only g-theta changes; the softmax head and cross-entropy loss stay the same.
svg.text: Four ways to get P(xj | x<j): counting, then a learned gθ
row 1 stores the distributions directly and fits them by counting (MLE) · rows 2–4 compute a vector hj from the prefix, then one shared softmax head
gθ: PREFIX → hj · rows 2–4: this is what changes
lookup table: one stored distribution per context
one shared head for the RNN and the Transformer
From row 2 on, only gθ changes. The softmax head and cross-entropy loss stay the same.
